title: Workforce shifts in two colonial regions
body: A researcher studies census data for two regions of British India over several decades. In Region X, a coastal area with growing ports and textile mills, the share of workers in agriculture fell from 72 per cent to 64 per cent, while the shares in manufacturing and services rose. In Region Y, an inland area with few mills and poor roads, the share of workers in agriculture rose from 70 per cent to 76 per cent over the same decades. For British India as a whole, agriculture's share of the workforce stayed at roughly 70-75 per cent throughout, with manufacturing near 10 per cent and services around 15-20 per cent.
